Synopsis:
Written by investment strategist Joachim Klement (Panmure Liberum), the piece argues that decades of efficiency-driven globalization have created structural vulnerabilities now being exposed by trade wars, COVID, and armed conflicts. Supply chain diversification and energy resilience are increasingly necessary but politically costly. The core tension: democratic governments face electoral incentives that discourage absorbing short-term pain for long-term strategic resilience, potentially ceding ground to less democratic, longer-horizon rivals.
